fieldMarks: Rams carry massive, curling horns that can weigh up to 14 kg; ewes have much smaller, only slightly curved horns.
Summer coat rich glossy brown, fading by late winter.
The desert subspecies is somewhat smaller with flatter, wider-spreading horns.
behavior: Gregarious: small groups of 8-10 are common, occasionally herds of over 100; mature rams live apart in bachelor groups most of the year.
Most populations move seasonally, using larger upland areas in summer and sheltered valleys in winter.
Mainly daytime feeders and largely grazers on grasses, sedges and forbs, taking browse when preferred foods are scarce.
Keen-sighted and able to spot movement up to about 1.6 km away; moves with ease on cliff ledges.
habitat: Alpine meadows, grassy mountain slopes and foothills close to rugged cliffs and bluffs, on drier slopes with limited snowfall. Winter range is typically about 760-1,520 m and summer range 1,830-2,590 m elevation.
range: Rocky Mountains from southern Canada to Colorado; desert bighorn from Nevada and California to west Texas and into Mexico.
